title: Pixi: an overkill for solo devs with AI?
author: lufereau
selftext:
I’d like to know your guys’ experience using pixi with AI for game dev. Pixi is known for being super performant but still a little verbose.
What tech are you using and which did you find it suits the best for AI to code?

comments.author: Over_Value1408
comments.body: Yes, Pixi might be overkill. Simple HTML elements with CSS are often enough, especially if AI is generating the code — it's faster to implement and easier to maintain.

comments.author: playful-developer
comments.body: I’m using pixi and claude code knows its way with it. I had to guide it a little bit when it came to svg graphics but that was it.

replies.author: lufereau
replies.body: My general experience with AI with Pixi is it always messing Pixi 7 with 8 and ruining performance with very frequent changes on graphics which I think is cpu based

replies.author: lufereau
replies.body:
not yet, i'm still a newbie on anything more advanced than the regular basics with AI. Although i've tried claude code, chatgpt, copilot with multiple agents, cursor... all of them end up messing this up.  
I got to a point where it stops haallucinating that much on it when i abstracted pixi more into a game engine

comments.author: darkwingfuck
comments.body:
Pixi is great, it’s not verbose for what it accomplishes, but use good software principles!

I would recommend making a render.js and that should be the ONLY file in your project that imports pixi. Abstract and wrap what you need, and then there is no verbosity. Then you can even port your program trivially.

replies.author: lufereau
replies.body: Yes I’m abstracting the hell out of it except for the transform operations and it’s been a better experience and less hallucinations from ai.
